key_insight: This paper shows that self-evolving multimodal models can become "agreeable" without truly looking at the image: they may optimize for answer consistency rather than visual grounding. The proposed takeaway is that training should explicitly encourage the decoder to attend to visual tokens, not just produce self-consistent text.
problem_solved: It addresses visual under-conditioning in self-evolving large multimodal models, where multi-role self-play and self-consistency rewards improve agreement but fail to ensure the model actually uses visual evidence.
method: Analyzes the failure mode of existing self-evolving LMMs, highlighting when answer agreement is driven by language priors instead of image understanding.
Introduces training or evaluation signals that emphasize attention to visual tokens, aiming to strengthen visual grounding during self-evolution.
Targets the decoder behavior directly so that self-consistent outputs are also visually conditioned, reducing hallucinated or image-agnostic responses.
impact: For practitioners, this means better multimodal models that are less likely to answer confidently from text priors alone. It is especially relevant for building more reliable unsupervised or self-improving vision-language systems.

paper_title: Paying More Attention to Visual Tokens in Self-Evolving Large Multimodal Models
paper_authors: Shravan Venkatraman, Ritesh Thawkar, Omkar Thawakar, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Hisham Cholakkal
